g.text: An eight-week public-furniture project guided by
Dyutiman Moulik, developed from ergonomic intent
through a full-scale mould and spatial visualisation.
Construct outdoor public furniture that is ergonomic,
works for all age groups and supports multiple seating
References focused on open forms, concrete mass,
timber warmth and the relationship between a resting
A sun-board scale model established the form. Metal
mesh was embedded for support, then white cement
with dyes was poured to preview the intended finish
The curved geometry was translated into a technical
drawing so form, thickness and construction could be
A full-scale CAD print was mapped directly onto the
build surface to position the mould and screw points
Truss work, reinforcement and mould preparation
tested how the sculptural object could be cast and
The final form was visualised as part of a public
space to pause, lounge, read or simply exist.
